Trump said in the interview‌ he “better not say” how many times he had spoken with Putin but touted ⁤a “good relationship” with⁣ his Russian counterpart.
The ⁢US ⁢president expressed hope that Putin’s war in Ukraine, which ‍is approaching its third anniversary,‍ ends ‍“fast.” He had previously vowed to end the conflict within 24 hours of taking office.
“I⁣ hope it’s fast. Every day people are dying. This ⁣war is so bad in Ukraine.‌ I want to end‌ this damn thing,” he told the New York Post.
Trump to Meet Zelensky and Putin Amid Progress in Ukraine Ceasefire⁤ Talks Washington, D.C. – ⁢In a important ⁣development, President Trump announced his‍ plans to meet with Ukrainian President⁤ Volodymyr Zelensky and Russian President Vladimir Putin in the coming week. The meetings come ‌as talks to end​ the ongoing conflict in Ukraine have reportedly made ample progress.
Progress in Ceasefire Talks
Earlier this week,‍ Trump expressed optimism about the progress in⁤ ceasefire talks. “Talks to⁤ end the‍ war have made a lot of progress,” Trump stated, highlighting the efforts to bring an end to the conflict that has claimed many ​lives⁤ on both sides.
Meetings Directed by Trump
During an interview conducted aboard⁣ Air Force One as Trump traveled ‍to​ Florida, he⁣ directed his national security⁤ adviser, Mike Waltz, to expedite the arrangements for these meetings. “They want to meet. Every⁤ day people are dying. Young handsome soldiers are being killed. Young men, like my⁤ sons. On both sides. all⁣ over the battlefield,” Trump emphasized, underscoring the urgency ‍of the situation.
Upcoming ​Meetings
Trump ‌confirmed ⁢that he ​would “probably” meet with President⁤ Zelensky next week and⁢ hinted‍ at a conversation with President Putin. “I will probably⁢ be ​meeting with President Zelensky next week, and​ I will probably⁤ be talking ⁢to President Putin,” Trump said, indicating a proactive approach‍ to resolving the conflict.
Munich Security Conference
Zelensky is expected to lead⁢ Ukraine’s delegation at‍ the Munich Security Conference, an event that will also see the attendance of Vice President JD Vance and special envoy for Ukraine and Russia Keith Kellogg. Notably, Trump will not be⁤ attending the conference.

Trump Proposes⁢ Rare earths Deal with Ukraine; Kremlin Silent on Potential‍ Putin Meeting In a recent statement‌ from the Oval⁣ Office,former President Donald Trump revealed ‍a transactional proposal aimed at securing Ukraine’s supply of rare earth minerals⁢ in exchange for continued US assistance. This move underscores Trump’s focus on leveraging strategic resources while maintaining ​US support for Ukraine amidst​ its⁢ ongoing conflict with Russia.
“We’re‍ looking to do a deal with Ukraine, were they’re‍ going to secure what we’re giving ‌them with their rare ⁤earths and ‌other things,” Trump ⁤told reporters, expressing his dissatisfaction with the ⁤level of aid provided ⁢by Europe compared to the US.
Insights into Trump’s Ukraine Strategy The proposal offers a glimpse⁣ into Trump’s ​intentions regarding the Ukraine war. Throughout his presidency, Trump had ‍been vocal about the financial‍ burden‍ the US faced in arming Kyiv.​ However, he had not provided detailed‌ plans on whether he would‌ continue or halt this support until now.
Kremlin’s Stance on Trump-Putin Meeting Meanwhile, the ⁣Kremlin has been tight-lipped ‍about any potential ​meeting ‍between Trump and Russian President‌ Vladimir Putin. According to Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov, there have been ‍no initial discussions regarding such a ⁤meeting.
“They haven’t had any‌ initial contact⁤ to discuss whether⁤ they need to meet or not and if they need, when and ⁣how,” Peskov told CNN’s matthew ⁢Chance.
Despite the Kremlin’s denial, there has been growing anticipation ⁤of contact ⁣between the two leaders. A senior Russian lawmaker recently stated that advanced preparations were underway for a meeting, possibly as early as this ‌month.

By securing these minerals, the US could bolster its⁢ technological⁣ edge and reduce ⁤dependence on other ​suppliers, such as China.
